In winter, Todaiji's Great Buddha Hall closes at 17:00 and Kasuga Taisha's inner area at 16:00. That's why most people see Nara in a rush and leave, and why one night there changes the whole visit 👇

🤔 Day trip or one night: which would you choose? Here's how we'd decide 👉 https://japanbystation.com/nara-day-trip-or-one-night

We checked every train time, fare and closing hour against Nara's visitor bureau, the temples and the railways before writing this.

🚆 THE TRAIN QUESTION

Kintetsu wins for most people. Osaka-Namba to Kintetsu-Nara takes about 40 minutes for ¥680, and the station is about 7 minutes' walk from Kofukuji. JR suits Rail Pass holders (the pass doesn't cover Kintetsu), but JR Nara is a longer walk from the park.

🦌 A DAY TRIP GIVES YOU

The big three on foot: Todaiji (¥800), the deer park and Kasuga Taisha, with kakinoha-zushi, sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves, for lunch near Todaiji. Arrive by 9:00 and it all fits before the gates close.

🌇 ONE NIGHT GIVES YOU

Sunset from Nigatsudo on the hill above the Great Buddha. Nara's own evening walking course goes from there down to Sarusawa Pond and ends with a drink at the bar of the Nara Hotel, open since 1909. Then a slow second morning in Isuien Garden and the old Naramachi streets.

💭 OUR TAKE

If you're moving between Kyoto and Osaka anyway, stay the night. Nara sits right between them on Kintetsu. With one base and only three or four nights, a day trip does the job.
